newsitem.title: UK: Orange confirmed winner in mobile race.
newsitem.headline: Orange confirmed winner in mobile race.

text.p: Orange Plc, Britain's youngest mobile telephone company, was on Thursday confirmed the winner in a battle among the four cellular rivals to net the most new customers.

Despite competitive new tariffs from its smaller rival One2One, jointly-owned by Cable and Wireless Plc and U S West Inc, Orange connected 86,000 net new customers compared to One2One's 80,000 in the second quarter of the year.

The two groups, which operate purely digital networks, had been expected to outrun their two more established rivals -- market leader Vodafone Group Plc and Cellnet, majority-owned by British Telecommunications Plc.

Vodafone and Cellnet are still migrating customers from their older analogue networks onto their digital networks and won a net new 53,000 and 74,000 subscribers respectively in the three months from April to June.
One2One, the last of the four to report subscriber figures, said on Thursday that it had won 27.4 percent of the net gain in growth and added that its customer base had now reached 700,000.
The group, which said that its share of the British market for mobile telephones had risen to 9.5 percent from 7.2 percent, now covers 85 percent of the country.

But, despite its recent new tariffs, which undercut similar offerings from its rivals, some analysts warn that cellular prices in Britain have much further to fall if the companies want to win new customers.
With most high-margin business customers already accounted for, the four now have to chase the less loyal, lower usage and less profitable residential market.

Despite recent moves to cut prices -- which have left those at the bottom end of the market almost a third lower than in April -- tariffs remain more than 30 percent higher than in the high-growth European countries where mobile penetration is high, analysts note.
